version.promotionalText: Open a video from Files and Dawn Player resumes it to the second, picks your audio and subtitle language for you, and plays MKV, HEVC and HLS with ease.
version.description:
Dawn Player plays the videos on your iPhone and the streams you already have, and it remembers how you like to watch them.

OPEN YOUR OWN FILES
Open a video straight from the Files app, from another app's share sheet, or with "Open a video file" inside Dawn Player. Videos opened from Files play where they are: nothing is copied and nothing is uploaded.

PICKS UP WHERE YOU STOPPED
Stop halfway through a film and it resumes to the second, even after you close the app or restart your phone. Everything you are part-way through, files and streams alike, waits in Continue Watching.

REMEMBERS YOUR LANGUAGE
Choose an audio language or a subtitle language once, and Dawn Player selects it automatically on every video that has it. Turn subtitles off and they stay off. Load your own .srt or .ass subtitle file for a video and it loads with that video every time you open it.

PLAYS ALMOST ANYTHING
Built on libmpv, the open-source playback engine behind some of the most capable desktop players. MKV, MP4, MOV, AVI, WebM and MPEG-TS; H.264, HEVC and more; HLS streams with multiple audio tracks and subtitle tracks. If a video's sound runs ahead of the picture, Audio sync fixes it in steps of 10 ms.

YOUR PLAYLISTS AND SERVERS
Add a playlist link or an .m3u / .m3u8 file, or sign in to a media server you already use. Dawn Player organises it into films and series, with artwork when the playlist provides it, a fast search, and a list of what you have saved for later.

MADE FOR WATCHING
Full-screen playback with gestures: double-tap to skip, swipe to seek, and swipe for brightness and volume. Audio can keep playing in the background. Send what you are watching to an Apple TV or another AirPlay device.

PRIVATE BY DESIGN
No account. No sign-up. No analytics, no advertising, no tracking. Your history, resume points and settings stay on your device, unless you choose to sync them through a server of your own.

INCLUDES NO CONTENT
Dawn Player is a media player. It does not include, sell or provide any videos, channels, playlists or subscriptions, and it does not help you find any. It plays only files on your device and sources you add yourself. Only add sources you have the right to access.

Terms: https://dawnplayer.com/terms.html
Privacy: https://dawnplayer.com/privacy.html

reviewDetail._comment: contactPhone is REQUIRED — verified, not assumed: the API answers 409 ENTITY_ERROR.ATTRIBUTE.REQUIRED and refuses to store review details at all without it. It must start with '+' and a country code (a second 409 says so), e.g. +31 6 12345678. These contact details go to App Review only; they are not shown on the product page, unlike Play's public developer contact.
reviewDetail.notes:
WHAT DAWN PLAYER IS

Dawn Player is a general-purpose video player for the user's own media. It ships with no content of any kind and has no catalogue, store, account or backend of its own. Out of the box it plays video files on the device; it can also play a playlist the user adds, or sign in to a media server the user already has an account with.

WHAT IS DIFFERENT IN THIS BUILD

- Video files on the device are now the first way in. The first screen offers, in this order: "Open a video file", "Add a playlist link or file", "Connect a media server". Dawn Player is registered for common video types (MP4, MOV, M4V, MKV, WebM, AVI, MPEG-TS) so a video can be opened from the Files app or another app's share sheet, in place, without copying.
- Resume survives restarts, including for files opened from Files: the app keeps a security-scoped bookmark, so the same file reopens at the same second.
- The audio and subtitle language the user picks is remembered and selected automatically on every later video that has it. External .srt/.ass subtitle files can be loaded for a video and are remembered for it.
- Playback is libmpv (the open-source mpv engine), not AVPlayer, so it plays MKV, HEVC, MPEG-TS and multi-audio HLS that the system player cannot.
- The Live tab no longer appears unless a source the user added actually contains live streams. Nothing in the app suggests, links to or helps find content.

HOW TO REVIEW (no login needed)

1. Launch the app.
2. Tap "Add a playlist link or file".
3. Paste this link into "Playlist link" and tap Connect:
   https://dawnplayer.com/demo/demo.m3u
4. Tap "Start watching", then the Movies tab. The playlist contains two films, both Creative Commons (CC BY 3.0, Blender Foundation) and both hosted by us:
   - Big Buck Bunny (2008), as an HLS stream
   - Sintel (2010), as an MKV file with subtitles in several languages
5. Play a film, leave it part-way, close the app and reopen it: it is in Continue Watching and resumes at the same position.
6. In Sintel, open Audio & subtitles and choose French subtitles. Open Sintel again: French is selected automatically.

To try a local file: save any video to Files, then use the share button in Files and choose Dawn Player, or tap the "Open a video file" icon at the top of Home.

The "Connect a media server" option signs in to a server the user already has an account with (address, username and password). It is not needed for this review, which is why no credentials are supplied.

APP TRANSPORT SECURITY

This build no longer sets NSAllowsArbitraryLoads. It sets only NSAllowsLocalNetworking (home servers on the user's own network) and NSAllowsArbitraryLoadsForMedia (AirPlay of a plain-HTTP stream the user added). Video playback, playlist downloads and artwork do not go through the URL loading system: libmpv and the app's networking layer open their own connections, so ATS does not apply to them. The app uses HTTPS whenever the user's source offers it.

PRIVACY

No account, no analytics, no advertising, no tracking and no crash reporting. Watch history and settings stay on the device. Optional sync is available only to a server the user runs themselves; it is off by default. Privacy policy: https://dawnplayer.com/privacy.html

CONTENT AND RIGHTS

Dawn Player does not host, sell, index or recommend content and has no relationship with any content provider. The add-source screen states that the app includes no content and that users must only add sources they have the right to access. Terms: https://dawnplayer.com/terms.html

Home can show lists of well-known titles (from Wikipedia page-view statistics, and from TMDB only with the user's own TMDB key), shown only where a title already exists in the user's own library.

ageRating._comment: Apple's 2025 questionnaire. Every attribute is required on every PATCH — omit one and the whole request 409s naming it. The frequency fields are strings (NONE / INFREQUENT_OR_MILD / FREQUENT_OR_INTENSE); ageAssurance and healthOrWellnessTopics look like frequency fields and are booleans. The load-bearing answer is unrestrictedWebAccess: the app opens arbitrary user-supplied stream URLs. Everything the app itself authors is NONE, because it authors nothing. Expect 17+ and do not argue it down.
